DeepSeek’s R1 release triggered the largest single-day loss in Nvidia’s history because it demonstrated that a frontier-class, open-weights reasoning model could be trained for a fraction of the cost previously assumed necessary [Source: ev-1]. Specifically, DeepSeek-R1 was released on January 20, 2025 [Source: ev-1], following its predecessor DeepSeek-V3 (released December 26, 2024), which reported training on roughly 2.79 million GPU-hours at a claimed cost of about US$5.6 million using export-restricted H800 chips [Source: ev-1]. This low-cost efficiency challenged the market thesis that demand for Nvidia’s hardware is moated by compute scale in frontier AI development [Source: ev-1]. Consequently, on January 27, 2025, Nvidia lost approximately US$589 billion in market capitalization, marking the largest single-day loss in stock-market history at the time, with about US$1 trillion erased across the tech complex as markets repriced this new economic reality [Source: ev-1].

The release revealed that scarcity driven by US export controls (specifically the H800 restrictions) had forced Chinese labs toward greater efficiency rather than preference driving their economics [Source: ev-1]. It highlighted that reinforcement learning techniques like GRPO and training methods such as R1-Zero (which used no supervised fine-tuning) could produce advanced reasoning capabilities without requiring the massive compute expenditures previously thought essential for frontier AI models [Source: ev-1].
